true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice; the first definition is dead code and its callers break

The file defines self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145 and then redefines self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149. In Ruby the second definition silently replaces the first, so the width/height variant can never be executed. Any existing caller still using the old signature breaks: a 5-argument call raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), and a 4-argument call downsize(from, to, w, h) silently mis-binds so the integer height lands in opts, where optimize then calls opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer. Remove the leftover 145-147 definition and update any remaining callers instead of shipping two.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side upload size check no longer honors max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb

validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; it now hardcodes 10 MB for every upload type. Letting images up to 10 MB through is the point of this feature (the server downsizes them), but attachments are not downsized by the new server code (it only touches FileHelper.is_image? files), so: (a) an admin who set max_attachment_size_kb below 10 MB loses client-side enforcement and nothing in create_upload re-validates attachment size, and (b) an admin who set it above 10 MB has users wrongly rejected by the client. Additionally the 413 handler at line 246 now always reports a 10 MB maximum in the error message, which is wrong whenever the web server or site setting has a different limit. The 10 MB cap should apply to images; attachments should still be validated against their own setting.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Animated downsize passes "80%" to gifsicle --resize-fit, which only accepts WxH geometry

downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated, producing `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's --resize-fit requires explicit WIDTHxHEIGHT pixel dimensions and does not understand ImageMagick-style percentages, so any animated downsize through this path exits non-zero and convert_with returns false without resizing. Previously the animated path only ever received "WxH" strings; the new percentage-based flow needs its own animated instructions (e.g. gifsicle --scale 0.8) or computed pixel dimensions.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize failures are ignored and the possibly-oversized original is uploaded anyway

The while loop stops after 5 attempts regardless of whether tempfile.size is now within SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, and nothing is logged when it returns false (e.g. when convert/gifsicle errors out). The possibly-still-oversized file then flows straight into Upload.create_for. A large image that resists reduction (very high resolution source, missing/broken ImageMagick) is therefore either silently stored far above the configured limit or fails later with an unrelated error. Check the size after the loop and log or reject when the attempts are exhausted.

Every 80% retry also runs the full ImageOptim pipeline on the intermediate file

Each loop iteration calls OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with, which runs ImageOptim.new.optimize_image! (jpegoptim/pngcrush/etc.) on the intermediate result, only for the next iteration to overwrite it. Worst case that is five full optimization passes per upload where one final pass would suffice; for multi-megabyte PNGs this adds tens of seconds of CPU in the deferred job and can push the synchronous API upload path (is_api? && params[:synchronous]) toward request timeouts. Resize without optimizing inside the loop and optimize once at the end.

Large animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame

The new auto-downsize code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...). OptimizedImage.optimize only selects the animated (gifsicle) instructions when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but uploaded tempfiles (e.g. /tmp/RackMultipart...) have no extension, so the check never matches the original filename or the file content. Large animated GIFs therefore go through `convert <path>[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame; the upload then succeeds with a static image and the user's animation is silently destroyed (previously the file was rejected for size and the user kept their original). The allow_animation option passed here is effectively dead for direct uploads; detect the format from the original filename or image content instead of the tempfile path.

No specs cover the new auto-downsize upload flow

The PR changes upload size enforcement on both client and server, adds a resize loop in create_upload, and changes OptimizedImage.downsize's signature, but no spec files are touched. Controller/model specs that upload an image larger than max_image_size_kb would catch the regressions visible here (animated GIFs flattened to one frame, the duplicate downsize definition, the loop storing oversized originals when attempts run out). The feature currently ships untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil

The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` twice unconditionally. The controller assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, so a request that omits the host param leaves `self.host` nil and `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError, turning a bad request into a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if self.host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.gsub(...)`, and rely on the format validation to reject blank values.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
update and destroy 500 on a nonexistent host id instead of 404

`update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then use it without a nil check: `save_host(host)` immediately does `host.host = ...` and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the id doesn't exist — e.g. an admin saves or deletes a row that another admin already removed in a different tab — this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 with no meaningful feedback instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find(params[:id])` (which renders 404 via rescuing RecordNotFound) or explicitly handle the nil case.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts keep http(s):// prefix and paths, so they silently stop matching

The old SiteSetting-based allowlist explicitly accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` (the removed code and its specs stripped the scheme before comparing), so real sites can have scheme-prefixed or path-bearing entries in the `embeddable_hosts` setting. The migration copies those values verbatim into the new table, but the new lookup `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares the stored value against the parsed hostname (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), and the model's scheme/path stripping lives in `before_validation`, which raw SQL inserts bypass. After upgrading, rows like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` never match, so comment embedding and feed import from those previously-working sites break without any error. Normalize the values (strip scheme and path, downcase) in the migration, mirroring the model's before_validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Fabricator files' contents are swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. The suite still passes because Fabrication registers fabricators by name regardless of file, but the file names are misleading and break the convention that a fabricator file defines the fabricator it's named after — anyone editing or searching for these will look in the wrong place. Swap the two files' contents.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration interpolates legacy host strings directly into raw SQL

Legacy hosts are inserted with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. Any host value containing a single quote (e.g. an apostrophe someone pasted into the old free-text setting) produces malformed SQL and aborts the migration mid-run, and it is an injection vector. Use bound parameters or `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)` when building the INSERT.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category setting row is missing or doesn't match a category

The migration computes the category id via `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories c INNER JOIN site_settings s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']`. site_settings rows only exist for settings an admin actually changed, so on any site that never set embed_category (or left it blank, or where the value doesn't exactly equal a category name) the query returns zero rows, `execute(...)[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError (PG::Result may also raise IndexError). The migration aborts, blocking the deploy — this will hit most existing sites since embedding is off by default, and fresh installs where site_settings is empty. The same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern is used for uncategorized_category_id on line 15. Check for an empty result before indexing and fall back to the uncategorized category.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

false_positives.candidate:
New admin endpoints have no request specs — only a subclass assertion

Both new controller specs (`admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert the controller is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. The feature's server API — creating, updating and deleting hosts, the uncategorized-category defaulting, validation-error responses for malformed hosts, and staff/admin permission enforcement — has no request coverage, so regressions (including the nil-host 500s in update/destroy) won't be caught. Add request specs exercising create/update/destroy with valid and invalid input and with non-admin users.

No uniqueness constraint on host — duplicates make category assignment ambiguous

`EmbeddableHost` validates only the format of `host`, and the migration adds no unique index. The new admin UI makes it easy to add the same host twice with different categories; `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then does `.where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, returning an arbitrary matching row, so which category embedded topics from that host land in becomes nondeterministic. Add `validates_uniqueness_of :host, case_sensitive: false` and ideally a unique index.

Plural branch of _hydrateEmbedded can leave undefined entries in the array

In the new `_ids` handling of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` is assigned directly to the model without any guard, whereas the singular `_id` branch only assigns `if (hydrated)`. `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined` when an id isn't present in the root payload (e.g. a sideloaded collection filtered by permissions), so the resulting property becomes `[undefined, ...]` and any later `.get()`/iteration over it will throw. Filter the mapped results (e.g. `hydrated.compact()`/`.filter(Boolean)`) or skip assignment when any id fails to resolve, matching the singular branch's behavior.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
NoMethodError (500) when the visitor has no TopicUser row

tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) can return nil. Emailed users normally have a row because send_notification_email calls TopicUser.change, but the unsubscribe URL is reachable by any logged-in user — someone who never interacted with the topic, or whose topic_users row was later removed — and the very next line calls tu.notification_level, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page. Guard the nil case or use TopicUser.change, which upserts.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change bookkeeping, allowing silent re-subscription

Assigning tu.notification_level and calling tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id are not updated and the notification_level_change MessageBus event is never published. One concrete consequence: TopicUser.update_last_read and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-subscribe users whose notifications_reason_id is null, and TopicUser.change would have stamped the reason as user_changed — because this code doesn't, a user who unsubscribes (set to regular) and later spends time reading the topic can be silently flipped back to tracking by the auto-track-on-view-time logic. Open browser tabs also won't reflect the new level in real time. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...) instead.

No specs for the new state-mutating topics#unsubscribe endpoint

The PR adds a new endpoint that mutates user state with several branches — watching/tracking → regular, regular/muted → muted, missing TopicUser row, slug-mismatch 301 redirect, login requirement — but adds no controller or request specs for it; the only spec change passes unsubscribe_url in message_builder_spec. Even basic coverage would have caught the nil-TopicUser 500 and the non-idempotent escalation to muted on repeat visits described above.

unsubscribe mutates notification state on an idempotent-unsafe GET topics#unsubscribe is wired to plain GET routes (config/routes.rb adds get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" and "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe") and it permanently writes the user's topic notification level before rendering the page. GET requests must not mutate state, and this one is not even idempotent: the first visit drops a watching/tracking user to regular, but simply reloading the confirmation page (or hitting back) executes the URL again and, because the level is now regular, falls into the else branch and fully mutes the topic — while the page still only claims 'You will stop receiving notifications'. It is also CSRF-able: any third-party page can embed and silently change a logged-in visitor's notification state, and any logged-in link prefetcher triggers it. The state change should happen via POST (the unsubscribe page already renders a topic-notifications-button the user can click), or the GET should render a confirmation without writing.

unsubscribe_link now hard-requires %{unsubscribe_url}, breaking other add_unsubscribe_link callers

The unsubscribe_link site text now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} ('To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})'), but Email::MessageBuilder only provides unsubscribe_url when the caller passes it in opts. The in-tree caller in user_notifications was updated, but any other caller of build_email with add_unsubscribe_link: true that doesn't pass unsubscribe_url (plugins, custom mailers) will now raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when building both the text body (MessageBuilder#body) and the HTML part (MessageBuilder#html_part), failing those emails entirely — the existing spec had to be changed for exactly this reason. Consider defaulting unsubscribe_url (e.g., to user_preferences_url) or making the second sentence conditional.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
match_count is incremented per validation pass, so one signup attempt is counted twice

should_block? has a database write side effect (match_count += 1 and save) and is invoked from EmailValidator, meaning it runs every time a User is validated. UsersController#create validates the user twice per attempt: once explicitly in `if user.valid? && SiteSetting.call_discourse_hub?` (users_controller.rb line 168) and again inside `user.save` (line 172). Because the record is new and unsaved, email_changed? is true for both passes, so a single blocked signup attempt increments match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at twice. Any other code that calls user.valid? and then user.save (or calls valid? as a dry-run check) also mutates these statistics. Match tracking should live outside the validation cycle (e.g. in the controller after a failed save) or otherwise be per-attempt rather than per-validation, otherwise the match_count/last_match_at audit data this feature exists to collect is unreliable.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, so a block is trivially bypassed

BlockedEmail.should_block? does an exact-match lookup: BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. On PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, and nothing normalizes case anywhere in the flow: User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] exactly as typed, BlockedEmail.set_defaults only sets action_type, and EmailValidator passes the raw value through. An admin who blocks spammer@example.com will not block Spammer@example.com or SPAMMER@example.com, even though those deliver to the same mailbox, so a blocked spammer can re-register simply by changing letter case. Normalize the address (e.g. strip + downcase) both when writing blocked_emails rows and when checking in should_block?, or query with a case-insensitive comparison such as lower(email) = lower(?). The added specs only exercise exact-case matches, so this gap is not covered by tests.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write

should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save. That is a read-modify-write: two concurrent requests matching the same blocked email can both read the same counter value, and one increment is silently lost. If these statistics are meant to be accurate, use an atomic update such as BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_counters(match_count: 1) plus an update of last_match_at, instead of incrementing an in-memory attribute and saving the whole record.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Unescaped URL interpolated into a single-quoted href in the imported footer TopicEmbed.import appends a footer to every imported post: #{url}. The only validation on url is a /^https?:\/\// prefix check, so a URL containing a single quote (e.g. from a malicious feed or a fetched page URL) breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML into the post body, which is then rendered raw via the raw_html cook path. Because the footer is appended after Readability extraction, this vector bypasses even the limited tag/attribute filtering that import_remote applies to article content. The URL should be HTML/attribute-escaped before interpolation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
i.content is nil for RSS items without content:encoded, crashing the hourly job

i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content:encoded/content element — plain RSS 2.0 feeds that only provide <description> are common, and SimpleRSS returns nil for absent elements. Because the job sets sidekiq_options retry: false, the exception kills the run silently until the next hour and any remaining items are never imported. Fall back to i.description (and/or i.summary) when content is absent. The new poll_feed_spec only exercises the site-setting gates and never parses a feed item, so this path is untested.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Blank embed_by_username silently no-ops, leaving an infinite reload/job loop

When SiteSetting.embed_by_username is blank, fetch_http looks up User.where(username_lower: '') and returns without creating anything or logging why. The embed controller then keeps rendering loading.html.erb, which reloads the iframe every 30 seconds and enqueues a new RetrieveTopic job on every reload — forever, for every open browser tab on the embedding site. The controller or retriever should fail fast with a clear error (or gate the embed on embed_by_username being configured) instead of looping silently.

Edits an already-deployed migration and adds force: true, which silently drops the table

This changes 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb — a migration that has already run in deployed environments — to create_table :top_topics, force: true. force: true issues DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so anywhere the table exists while the migration is considered pending (db:schema:load followed by migrate, restored backups, staging/dev databases) the existing top_topics table is silently dropped and recreated. Where the migration already ran, the edit has no effect at all, making it misleading. Old migrations should not be edited; the new create_topic_embeds migration also does not need force: true.

Feed HTML is stored and rendered completely unsanitized (stored XSS)

Feed item content is imported with no sanitization: poll_feed unescapes entities via CGI.unescapeHTML, then TopicEmbed.import stores the string as the post raw with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts. The result is rendered unsanitized both on the forum (the app renders post.cooked unescaped, trusting the normal cooking pipeline to have sanitized it) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb via <%= raw post.cooked %>, which is served from the Discourse origin inside the iframe. Any <script> or event handler attribute in a feed entry — from a hostile or compromised blog/feed, a rogue author on a multi-author blog, or a MITM on a plaintext feed URL — becomes stored XSS executing in the forum origin as viewing users/admins. CGI.unescapeHTML makes it worse by converting the feed's safely entity-escaped markup into live tags. Imported content must be sanitized (e.g., with the already-bundled sanitize gem) before being stored as raw HTML.

Unauthenticated endpoint triggers remote fetch and topic creation; referer check is trivially spoofable

GET /embed/best enqueues a RetrieveTopic job for any embed_url with no existing embed, with no authentication and no rate limiting. The only gate is that the Referer host matches embeddable_host, which any non-browser client can spoof (curl -H 'Referer: http://blog.example.com' ...). The 60-second Redis throttle in TopicRetriever is per-URL, so an attacker can supply unlimited distinct URLs on the embeddable host: each one makes the server fetch that page and create a forum topic as the embed_by_username user (topic spam, bandwidth/CPU amplification), and when feed_polling_enabled is on each request also triggers a synchronous full PollFeed run inside the job. Consider per-IP rate limiting and/or restricting which paths are importable.

X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value

ALLOWALL is not a permitted X-Frame-Options value (the spec defines DENY, SAMEORIGIN, and ALLOW-FROM uri). Browsers currently ignore unrecognized values, which is why framing happens to work, but the behavior is undefined and stricter user agents or normalizing proxies may handle it differently. To allow cross-origin framing for this action, remove the X-Frame-Options header instead of setting an invalid value.

add_column with default on posts rewrites the whole table under an exclusive lock

add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false causes PostgreSQL (pre-11) to rewrite every row of the posts table to materialize the default, holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration. posts is typically the largest table in a Discourse database, so on busy installs this migration can block all writes to posts for minutes during deploy. Add the column without a default/NOT NULL, backfill in batches, then apply the default and constraint.

embed.js/embed.css are never added to config.assets.precompile — feature 404s/500s in production

The PR adds app/assets/javascripts/embed.js and app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and references them via stylesheet_link_tag 'embed' (in the embed layout) and as the script embedding sites load, but no config change adds 'embed.js' or 'embed.css' to the asset precompile list. With the application's explicit precompile list and assets.compile disabled in production, /embed/best will raise AssetNotPrecompiledError and the embed snippet URL will 404, so the entire feature is broken in production. Add both assets to config.assets.precompile.

embeddable_host is compared as an exact string against URI#host with no normalization

The check URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host compares the parsed host against free-form admin text. Values admins commonly paste — 'http://example.com', 'example.com/', or 'example.com:8080' — never equal URI#host ('example.com'), so every legitimate embed is rejected with 'invalid referer host' and no diagnostics. The same strict comparison in TopicRetriever.invalid_host? also fails when the blog's canonical URL host differs from the page host (www vs apex), producing the infinite loading screen. Parse/normalize the setting (compare host and port explicitly, and consider allowing subdomains) or validate its format when saved.

open(url) used without requiring open-uri on the retrieve path

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url), but this file never requires 'open-uri' — only poll_feed.rb does. The HTTP-retrieve path (EmbedController → RetrieveTopic job → TopicRetriever#fetch_http → TopicEmbed.import_remote) therefore only works if Jobs::PollFeed happened to be loaded already; in lazy-loading environments (dev/test, or any process that never referenced PollFeed) Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT. Add require 'open-uri' to topic_embed.rb (or lib/topic_retriever.rb) so the dependency is explicit.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items mixin passes standard keywords verbatim to legacy properties that use different value names

The new `align-items($alignment)` mixin copies its argument into `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`, but those legacy properties do not accept the standard `flex-start`/`flex-end` keywords — they expect `start`/`end`. The mixin compiles silently and the declaration is simply dropped by those engines, so the first time someone uses `@include align-items(flex-start)` (the most common value in real layouts) alignment will be silently broken in old WebKit and IE10. Current usages only pass `center`/`baseline`, which happen to be valid in both syntaxes, so this is latent rather than an active bug — but the mixin should map the values (or the limitation should be documented) since it is being introduced for codebase-wide reuse. Additionally, `-ms-align-items` on line 121 is not a property that exists in any browser (IE10's 2012 spec only has `-ms-flex-align`), so that line is dead code.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. The translate accelerator loads translations lazily per locale: I18n.translate only calls load_locale(config.locale), and nothing outside the controller (Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer such as notification/digest emails, rake tasks, console) ever loads the fallback locales. So when a key is missing in the user's locale in one of those contexts, the I18n::Backend::Fallbacks module iterates the fallback chain but the backend holds no data for the default locale or :en (their yml files were never read), and the output is "translation missing: ..." instead of the English text. This is exactly the case the feature is meant to fix, and emails are a primary surface for it. The ensure_loaded! call should live in the translation path itself (e.g. have I18n.ensure_loaded!/load_locale load the whole fallback chain for the locale) or be invoked from job/mailer entry points, not solely from ApplicationController.

No tests for the new paginator, the negative-offset path, or the endpoint's optimized branch

The PR adds a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class, a user-reachable branch in the audit log endpoint, and a behavioral change to BasePaginator.get_result that affects all cursor-paginated endpoints, but adds no tests. Both new code paths fail on first use (the datetime TypeError in get_item_key and the negative-slice AssertionError), which a single happy-path test of GET /organizations/{slug}/audit-logs/?optimized_pagination=true would have caught, and the BasePaginator change has no coverage for prev/negative-offset cursors either.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
"Advanced" negative-offset pagination always 500s: Django rejects negative slices

In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is set and the client supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts e.g. "0:-5:0"), the code evaluates queryset[cursor.offset : cursor.offset + limit + extra]. Django's QuerySet raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported") for negative slice bounds, so the request errors with a 500. The comments above the branch are false: Django does not "properly handle negative slicing automatically", and the statement "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level" is meaningless. This advertised feature cannot work as written and is reachable via a crafted cursor query parameter on the audit log endpoint.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes with TypeError when used with datetime ordering

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key is copied from the numeric Paginator and does math.floor/math.ceil on the raw attribute value. Its only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, uses it with order_by="-datetime", so the value is a datetime and math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every non-empty page, so any request with optimized_pagination=true that returns at least one audit log row will 500. Additionally, value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor value, so even if the first page worked, page 2 would compare a timestamp column against a float in the extra WHERE clause and raise a database error. The class needs DateTimePaginator-style key conversion (or should subclass DateTimePaginator). No test covers this path, which is why it wasn't caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In BasePaginator.get_result(), when cursor.is_prev is True, it sets start_offset = offset without clamping, allowing negative offset values to be passed to queryset slicing.
Accessing .has_global_access on organization_context.member can raise an AttributeError when organization_context is None, particularly for non-superuser non-member users.

false_positives.candidate:
Added comment falsely claims negative cursor offsets are supported

The new comment in Cursor.__init__ says "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios", but no code was changed and negative offsets are not actually usable: Django querysets raise ValueError on negative slices, and BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0. This misdocuments the Cursor contract for anyone building on it and should be removed or corrected.

No test coverage for the eviction feature or the new paginator

The headline behavior of this PR — capping segments at 1000 spans via ZPOPMIN during insert — has no test: the buffer tests were only updated to add the newly required end_timestamp_precise field. A test inserting more than 1000 spans into one segment should assert which spans survive (lowest end_timestamp_precise evicted), that the segment still flushes, and that TTLs are intact. Likewise, the new OptimizedCursorPaginator / audit-log optimized_pagination path has no tests at all; even a trivial smoke test would have caught that it 500s on the first page due to the datetime TypeError.

Redirect resolution limit lowered 10000 to 1000; deep traces will silently split into multiple segments

The redirect-following loop limit was reduced from 10000 to 1000 and the comment documenting the consequence ("segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly") was deleted. For trace trees deeper than 1000 redirects, the loop now stops early and the span is written to whatever set the partial resolution landed on, splitting one logical segment into multiple flushed segments (partial/duplicated output downstream). This tradeoff is 10x more reachable than before; if intentional for script latency, the consequence should stay documented and a metric should be emitted when the limit is actually hit.

SET to ZSET type change on existing span-buf:s:* keys will cause WRONGTYPE errors during rolling deploys

The PR changes the Redis type of the existing span-buf:s:{project_id:trace_id}:span_id keys from SET (sadd/sscan/sunionstore/scard) to ZSET (zadd/zscan/zunionstore/zcard/zpopmin) while keeping the exact same key names. Segment keys live up to redis_ttl (3600s) and consumers are upgraded in a rolling fashion, so old and new code will operate on the same keys concurrently: old consumers' SADD/SSCAN against newly created ZSET keys, and new consumers' ZADD/ZCARD/ZPOPMIN/ZSCAN against SET keys created minutes earlier, both raise redis WRONGTYPE errors. That crashes span processing and flushing and drops spans. The migration needs a new key prefix or an explicit transition plan rather than reusing the live keyspace.

Spans evicted by ZPOPMIN are dropped silently with no metric or log

When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the script now evicts the excess with ZPOPMIN, permanently discarding span payloads from the segment. The previous behavior (skip oversized segments at flush time) emitted the metric spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded and an error log; that check is removed from _load_segment_data in this PR, and the new eviction emits nothing: the script doesn't return the evicted count and process_spans records no metric. Operators lose all visibility into truncated segments and the associated data loss. Return the evicted count from the script and emit a metric/log from Python.

max_segment_spans option is now dead; the cap is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua

SpansBuffer.__init__ still accepts and stores max_segment_spans (default 1001), but the only remaining enforcement is a hardcoded `if span_count > 1000` in add-buffer.lua. The flush-time check that used self.max_segment_spans was removed from _load_segment_data, so configuring this option now silently does nothing (and the default 1001 doesn't even match the Lua 1000). Either pass the limit into the script as an ARGV or delete the parameter.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling eligibility is computed from the outer `dataset` and raw request query instead of the scoped dataset and query actually executed

Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, ...)`, the eligibility check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` using the closure variable `dataset` from `get()`, not the `scoped_dataset` argument, and `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`/`_is_error_focused_query` re-read `request.GET["query"]` instead of the `query` argument. The dashboard-widget split path calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., split_query, ...)` where `split_query` is rewritten to `(<query>) AND !event.type:transaction`; that error-only query is never upsampled because the decision was made against the original (metrics) dataset and the unmodified request query. The transform decision should be based on the dataset and query string actually being executed, otherwise upsampling is silently skipped (or could be misapplied) for exactly the requests the function arguments describe.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental git submodule (gitlink) added without .gitmodules

The PR adds a file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290...`, i.e. a git submodule/gitlink pointing at the base commit of this same repository, but no `.gitmodules` entry is added. This is almost certainly an accidental commit of a nested checkout. It breaks any workflow that initializes submodules: `git submodule update --init` fails with `fatal: no submodule mapping found in .gitmodules for path 'sentry-repo'`, which affects CI checkouts that run with `--recurse-submodules` and fresh clones. It should be removed from the PR.

Cache key built with Python hash() of project ids is collision-prone

The eligibility cache key is `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Python's `hash()` is not collision-free: two different project-id sets within the same organization can produce the same hash and therefore share a cache entry, causing the wrong allowlist eligibility (and thus wrong counts) to be served for up to 60 seconds. The key should encode the ids directly (e.g. comma-joined sorted ids) rather than a hash digest of them.

No tests for the caching behavior that is the PR's stated performance optimization

The unit tests only exercise the private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`); the main entry point `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — which contains the new 60-second cache, the cache key construction, and the interaction between cached eligibility and the per-request dataset/query check — is never called. Cache hit/miss behavior, the TTL, and stale-cache regressions (the headline "performance optimization" of this PR) are therefore completely unverified.

_is_error_focused_query substring-matches event.type:error, misfiring on negations and quoted text

`_is_error_focused_query` decides whether to rewrite `count()` into `sum(sample_weight)` by checking `if "event.type:error" in query.lower()`. This substring test ignores search semantics: a discover query like `!event.type:error` (the standard way to select transaction-like events) contains the substring and will be treated as error-focused, so its `count()` is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) over non-error rows that have no sample_weight — returning NULL/incorrect counts. A free-text search such as `message:"event.type:error"` also false-positives. For allowlisted projects this silently returns wrong data on common discover queries; the check should parse the query and inspect the actual event.type filter (including its negation) rather than doing a substring match.

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code; allowlist changes have no invalidation path

`invalidate_upsampling_cache(organization_id, project_ids)` is introduced with a docstring saying it "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes", but nothing in this PR (or elsewhere) calls it, and there is no signal/hook wired to the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. As shipped, every allowlist change takes up to the full 60-second TTL to take effect with no supported way to invalidate. Either wire the invalidation to the option update path or remove the unused helper and rely on the documented TTL.

upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) without coalescing NULLs, silently undercounting unsampled errors

The new `upsampled_count` SnQL function is defined as `toInt64(sum(Column("sample_weight")))`. In snuba, `sample_weight` on the errors/discover storage is Nullable and is only populated for error events that carry a client sample rate; error events ingested before a project was allowlisted, from SDKs that don't sample, or server-side have NULL `sample_weight`. ClickHouse `sum()` ignores NULL rows and returns NULL if every row is NULL, so (a) any unsampled error events are silently excluded from the returned count (e.g. 10 unsampled errors + 1 error sampled at 0.1 returns 10 instead of the correct 20), and (b) a time bucket containing only unsampled events returns NULL/0 instead of the true count. The added tests never exercise events without a client_sample_rate, so this is not caught. The aggregate should treat missing weights as 1, e.g. `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))`; the code comment's assumption that sample_weight always exists for allowlisted projects is not guaranteed by the schema.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns IDs with nodestore data when entries are missing

`fetch_error_details` builds pairs with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` and filters with `if data is not None`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits entries whose data is missing (e.g., expired events). When any entry is dropped, `events.values()` is shorter than `error_ids`, so the zip shifts: an error ID gets paired with a *different* event's data, and the trailing IDs are silently dropped — the `if data is not None` filter cannot realign them. The result is `ErrorEvent` objects whose `id` does not correspond to their `title`/`message`/`timestamp`. Today `id` is not consumed downstream (only title/message/timestamp reach the Seer prompt), so the visible impact is latent, but the mapping is incorrect and any future use of `id` (and any debugging of these payloads) will be wrong. Iterate `node_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data

In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` organization feature is enabled, the new branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` — completely ignoring the actual query results (`result.data`, `fields`, `eventView`, etc.) that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` path uses. `columns={[]}` also means no column headers are generated (the component's fallback of deriving columns from `meta.fields` gets an empty object too). Any organization that has this feature flag turned on will see every table widget on dashboards render as an empty table with no rows and no headers, instead of their data. The new visualization needs to be wired to the real table results before the flag can be enabled, or this branch should not ship.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness and age allows negatives

`validate_timestamp` rejects only when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy (and `validate_age` mirrors this for `timestamp`). A report containing both `timestamp` and `age: 0` passes validation even though the intent is that the two fields are mutually exclusive, because `0` is falsy. `age: 0` is a legitimate value for a report delivered immediately. Additionally, the `age` field is declared as `serializers.IntegerField(required=False)` with no `min_value`, while `timestamp` has `min_value=0`, so negative ages are accepted. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` (and add `min_value=0` to `age`) so the spec constraint is actually enforced.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
Truthy check on custom cell renderer discards valid falsy React nodes

In `renderDefaultBodyCell` (and identically in `renderDefaultHeadCell` at line 32), the override is applied via `const cell = renderTableBodyCell?.(...); if (cell) { return cell; }`. The documented contract (in `tableWidgetVisualization.tsx` and the stories) is that returning `undefined` from a custom renderer triggers the fallback. With a truthiness check, a custom renderer that returns other valid falsy React nodes — `null` (to intentionally render nothing), `0`, or `''` — will be silently discarded and replaced by the default field renderer. This means a custom body/head cell renderer cannot render an empty cell. The check should be `if (cell !== undefined)` to match the documented contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code single-use guarantee is not enforced under concurrent requests

Code consumption is a read-modify-write: decrypt the stored array, indexOf the supplied code, set that slot to null, re-encrypt and update the user row — with no transaction, lock, or conditional update. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same valid backup code can both read the array before either writes, both pass indexOf, and both be authenticated, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' promise made in the UI copy (backup_code_instructions). A transaction or an atomic update would close the window.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup codes are shown exactly once with no recovery path, and the dialog can be dismissed at that step

handleEnable() enables 2FA on the server and only then moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step. At that step the dialog can still be closed without using the Close/Copy/Download buttons (dialog close control / Escape / overlay via onOpenChange), and resetState() is only wired to the Cancel and Close buttons, not to onOpenChange — so component state is also left stale (step stays DisplayBackupCodes with the old codes). The codes are never retrievable again: the totp/setup endpoint rejects users who already have twoFactorEnabled, and this PR adds no regeneration UI or API. A user who closes the wizard before saving the codes (and likewise all users who enabled 2FA before this feature and have backupCodes=null) has no way to obtain codes, and is locked out if they later lose their authenticator. Completion should be gated on an explicit confirmation and/or a regenerate-codes endpoint should exist.

Backup-code login is rejected for users whose identityProvider is not CAL

The guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` runs before the new backup-code branch. A Google/SAML user with twoFactorEnabled who submits a backup code (and therefore no totpCode) gets the 'account created with identity provider' error instead of having the backup code verified — the condition was not extended to also allow `credentials.backupCode`. This user class is real: the signIn callback converts CAL accounts to Google/SAML while keeping twoFactorEnabled and backupCodes, and then routes them through the /auth/login?totp= (loginWithTotp) flow. It is compounded by apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx, which renders ExternalTotpFooter (no 'Lost access' button) for that flow, so these users have no way to use their backup codes at all and are permanently locked out if they lose their authenticator.

No test exercises logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA with one

The added e2e steps only verify that the backup-codes screen renders, the download filename, and the copy toast. The core behavior of the feature — a successful login with a backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use consumption (the code is invalidated after use in next-auth-options.ts), and disabling 2FA with a backup code — has no automated coverage, and the PR checklist explicitly states tests proving the feature works were not added. A regression in the authorize or disable logic would ship unnoticed.

Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order in the shared PasswordField

Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button removes it from the tab order in every place the shared PasswordField is used (login, password change, 2FA setup/disable, etc.). Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the control to verify what they typed, which is an accessibility regression for a security-relevant input. If the intent was to fix tab order into the 2FA digit inputs of one specific form, the change should be scoped to that form rather than the shared component.

missing_backup_codes message tells users to generate codes in settings, which is impossible

The string "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown when a 2FA-enabled user has no stored backup codes — i.e. every user who enabled 2FA before this feature — both in the login flow and in the disable-2FA modal. No settings UI or API exists to generate backup codes after initial setup (the setup endpoint rejects already-enabled users), so the instruction cannot be followed; users who lost their authenticator are directed to a nonexistent capability instead of being told to disable/re-enable 2FA or contact support.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent fallback when externalCalendarId is missing is dead code, yielding undefined calendarId

`const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — the fallback branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, which can never match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined. Previously the fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which let updates for older bookings (booking references without externalCalendarId) still target the destination calendar. Now those updates call `calendar.events.update` with `calendarId: undefined` and fail (e.g. rescheduling pre-existing bookings). The same dead fallback pattern exists in deleteEvent (line ~317), where it silently degrades to the "primary" calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated change inverts IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for organization slug

This PR changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting when the organization's `slug` column is written. Previously the slug was set only when team billing was disabled, and `requestedSlug` metadata was used when billing was enabled; now organizations created with billing disabled never get a `slug` (breaking their org subdomain/URL), while billing-enabled instances write `slug` directly, bypassing the requested-slug verification flow. This change is unrelated to the destinationCalendar work and appears to have been pulled in accidentally.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
Crash when a Google Meet event has no destination calendar

In EventManager.create(), the code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When the event has no destination calendar (null or empty array — e.g. an organizer without a connected destination calendar booking an event type whose location is Google Meet), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, failing the entire booking creation. The previous code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) safely fell back to Cal Video in exactly this case. Restore the optional chain: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

Hangout-link patch uses possibly-undefined calendarId

In createEvent, the insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"` but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that writes the hangout link into the event description passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly. When no destination calendar matches the credential (selectedCalendar is undefined, which the new credentialId-based lookup allows), the patch is issued with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link never gets added to the event description. Use the same `|| "primary"` fallback as the insert.

No tests cover the new multi-host calendar fan-out

The PR's central behavior change — createAllCalendarEvents creating one calendar event per destination calendar (including fetching other hosts' credentials from the DB) and updateAllCalendarEvents iterating multiple calendar references — has no unit or integration coverage; the only test change is an updated webhook payload expectation. Given this touches booking creation, reschedule, and cancellation for every calendar provider, at least one test exercising a collective booking with two hosts (verifying two references with correct credentialId/externalCalendarId, and that cancel/reschedule cleans up both) should be added.

Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference per booking

In the recurring + allRemainingBookings branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` takes only the first calendar reference of each updated booking. Now that collective bookings store one calendar reference per host, cancelling a recurring collective booking deletes only one host's calendar event per occurrence and leaves the other hosts' events orphaned on their calendars. Additionally, because this block now sits inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, it re-runs once per calendar reference of the cancelled booking, issuing duplicate delete attempts. Iterate all calendar references of each updated booking instead.

References created via updateLocation lose credentialId and externalCalendarId

updateLocation's referencesToCreate now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but CalendarManager.updateEvent results never populate those fields, so every booking reference created through the edit-location flow is stored with null credentialId/externalCalendarId (previously they fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar`'s values). editLocation.handler persists these via `references: { create: ... }`, and later cancel/reschedule flows can no longer map these references to the correct credential and calendar — in multi-host bookings this means those calendar events can't be updated or deleted. Either have updateEvent return the reference's credentialId/externalCalendarId or keep the previous fallback.

Team members' destination calendars are dropped when organizer/event type has none

`evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops, silently discarding the collected team calendars. For a collective event where the organizer has no destination calendar but other hosts do, no calendar events are created for anyone (EventManager falls into its no-destination fallback path). Initialize to `[]` instead of `null` so the team hosts' calendars are always included.

Video references no longer store credentialId, so meetings are not deleted on cancel

In create(), referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Previously non-calendar (video) results used `result.credentialId`, which createMeeting populates. With credentialId now persisted as null for video references, handleCancelBooking's check `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` fails, so the video meeting (Zoom, etc.) is never deleted when the booking is cancelled — an orphaned meeting link remains valid. Keep passing `result.credentialId` for video results.

createEvent always targets the main host's calendar, breaking multi-host events on Office365

createEvent takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]` and posts to `/me/calendars/{externalId}/events`. With collective events, EventManager now calls createEvent once per host credential, passing the full destinationCalendar array each time. For every host other than the organizer, `destinationCalendar[0]` is still the organizer's calendar, so the Graph API call uses this host's access token against a calendar ID belonging to a different user (or a non-Office365 calendar ID if the organizer uses another provider) — the request fails and that host never receives the event on their calendar. Like GoogleCalendarService now does, this should pick the destination calendar whose `credentialId` matches the credential being used (falling back to `/me/calendar/events`).

createEvent uses the first destination calendar instead of the current host's calendar

createEvent/createAttendees derive `calendarId` from `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. For collective bookings EventManager invokes createEvent once per host credential with the full array, so for any host other than the organizer the Lark API calls are made with that host's token against the organizer's calendar ID, which belongs to a different Lark account and will fail — the non-organizer host gets no calendar event. It should select the destination calendar matching the credential in use rather than always the first element.

loadUsers masks unexpected errors and leaks Prisma messages as 400s

The new try/catch in loadUsers converts PrismaClientKnownRequestError into an HTTP 400 with the raw Prisma error message (exposing internal database error details to clients) and converts every other unexpected error into a generic 500 "Unable to load users", discarding the original error and making production failures undebuggable. Additionally, an empty dynamicUserList previously simply returned no users but now throws a 500. Consider letting errors propagate as before.

loadUsers no longer selects organization slug for dynamic bookings

The rewritten loadUsers drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user (no eventTypeId) query that existed before this change. Any downstream logic relying on `user.organization.slug` for dynamic collective bookings (e.g. org-domain booker URLs) now receives undefined. If the removal wasn't deliberate, restore the select.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
minimumTokenResponseSchema drops every field except access_token, corrupting stored credentials when sync is enabled

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (Zod schemas have no meaningful toString), so the intended catch-all does not exist — the second key simply overwrites the first. Combined with zod's default behaviour of stripping unknown keys, parsing any token response with this schema keeps only `access_token` and discards expires_in/expires_in-like fields, scope, instance_url, etc. Consequences when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on: zoom stores `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined * 1000 = NaN` (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts line 122) so the token can never be considered valid again; salesforce (which always uses this parser when the flag is on, even though it calls Salesforce directly) permanently loses instance_url from the stored key, breaking future connections; office365 keeps a stale expiry. Zod's .catchall()/.passthrough() or an explicit expiry field is needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Calendar credential key is overwritten with the zod SafeParse wrapper object instead of the parsed tokens

parseRefreshTokenResponse() returns the whole zod safeParse result ({ success: true, data: {...} }), not the parsed data. Here it is assigned to `key` and written straight into the DB via prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } }), so after the first token refresh the stored credential key becomes {"success": true, "data": {access_token: ...}}. true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body), JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) (lines 57-59) are called without try/catch — a malformed body, bad ciphertext or a mismatched CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws and results in an unhandled 500 (potentially with stack trace) instead of a 400. false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the credential-sync webhook or the token-refresh sync path

The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. The new endpoint can overwrite any user's stored third-party tokens, and the refreshOAuthTokens/parseRefreshTokenResponse utilities sit on the critical path of every calendar/video integration — a broken response shape here corrupts credentials in the DB (several such issues exist in this PR). At minimum, tests should cover: valid/invalid webhook secret, malformed and undecryptable payloads, create vs update behaviour, apps with multiple credentials per user, and both branches (sync enabled/disabled) of the refresh helpers.

Sync-path token refresh stores expiry_date = now and drops refresh_token/email from the credential key

When credential sync is enabled, the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry (per the contract documented in refreshOAuthTokens.ts), so `responseBody.expires_in` is undefined and `expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + (responseBody?.expires_in || 0) * 1000)` becomes the current time — the token is considered expired on the very next getToken() call, so every MS Teams API call triggers another refresh request to the sync endpoint. Additionally `key: responseBody` replaces the entire stored credential key, discarding refresh_token and email; if sync is later disabled the credential can no longer be refreshed. The refreshed fields should be merged into the existing key and the expiry read from whatever the endpoint actually returns.

Webhook overwrites an arbitrary credential when a user has several for the same app, and find-then-create is racy

Cal.com allows a user to hold multiple credentials for the same appId (e.g. two Google accounts) and teams to hold their own. `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` picks whichever row happens to come first and overwrites its key with the pushed tokens, potentially replacing account A's tokens with account B's and silently breaking that connection; team credentials are never matched at all. Additionally the find-then-update/create sequence is not atomic and Credential has no unique constraint on (userId, appId), so two concurrent webhook deliveries for a new credential both find nothing and create duplicates. The payload should identify the exact credential (or the endpoint should enforce a uniqueness constraint and use a transaction/upsert).

Webhook secret compared with a plain !== string comparison

The shared secret is verified with `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, a non-constant-time comparison that is susceptible to timing attacks. For a secret that alone grants the ability to write arbitrary third-party tokens for any user, use crypto.timingSafeEqual (after length checks) instead.

appStoreMetadata is keyed by directory name, not App.slug, so the webhook 404s for most major apps

The lookup `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` assumes the metadata map is keyed by the App table slug, but it is keyed by app-store directory names: `zoomvideo`, `googlecalendar`, `office365calendar`, `office365video`, `larkcalendar` — while the corresponding App slugs are `zoom`, `google-calendar`, `office365-calendar`, `msteams`, `lark-calendar` (see e.g. office365video using getAppKeysFromSlug("msteams") and createOAuthAppCredential({ appId: "zoom" }) in this PR). For those apps the metadata lookup returns undefined and the endpoint responds 404, making credential sync unusable for Google Calendar, Office 365, MS Teams, Zoom and Lark. The mapping from app slug to the metadata key needs to be resolved differently (e.g. match on metadata type/appId).

prisma is used but never imported, breaking the build

The newly added refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` at line 96, but the file's imports (lines 1-20) do not include `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This is a TypeScript compile error (Cannot find name 'prisma') that will fail type-check/build for the app-store package.

Guest email matching is case-sensitive, bypassing the blacklist and duplicate checks

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased (line 71) but the incoming guest is compared un-normalized (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so 'Blocked@Example.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'blocked@example.com'. The existing-attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) and the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check in sendAddGuestsEmails have the same problem, so a case-variant of an existing attendee's email creates a duplicate Attendee row, and isAttendee (line 52) can fail to recognize an attendee whose stored email case differs from their account email. Emails should be normalized (e.g. lowercased) before all comparisons. Additionally, the input array itself is never de-duplicated server-side — the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog's zod schema — so a direct API call containing duplicate entries creates duplicate attendees.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner permission check uses && instead of ||

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`. isTeamOwner is only true for users with the OWNER membership role, so any team admin who is not also the team owner fails this check and gets a FORBIDDEN ('you_do_not_have_permission') error when calling viewer.bookings.addGuests. The variable name, and the fact that the bookings UI exposes the 'Additional guests' action to team admins, indicate the intent was OR. Consequence: team admins can open the Add Guests dialog but every submission fails.

sendAddGuestsEmails decides which template each attendee receives via `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, but the handler passes the original `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests`. If the request includes an address that already belongs to an existing attendee (which uniqueGuests deliberately filtered out, e.g. the organizer re-submitting an existing guest), that existing attendee is treated as 'new' and receives a full booking-confirmation email (AttendeeScheduledEmail) instead of the 'new guests added' notification.

The existing-attendee dedupe (`guest === attendee.email`) and the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` check in sendAddGuestsEmails have the same problem, so a case-variant of an existing attendee's email creates a duplicate Attendee row, and isAttendee (line 52) can fail to recognize an attendee whose stored email case differs from their account email. Emails should be normalized (e.g. lowercased) before all comparisons. Additionally, the input array itself is never de-duplicated server-side — the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog's zod schema — so a direct API call containing duplicate entries creates duplicate attendees.
